item.title: Independent Assessment of AI R&D Acceleration at Anthropic in October 2026 (METR)
item.description: The first outside audit of whether a frontier lab is using its own AI to speed up AI research. With staff interviews, surveys and Anthropic's internal benchmark index, METR estimates Anthropic now improves its models on well-specified tasks about twice as fast as in 2024-25 (plausibly 1.3x to 3x), finds that training compute growth did not accelerate, and judges that about 80 percent of the speed-up comes from AI itself. It is also candid about the limits: Anthropic redacted most of the evidence METR found most informative. A first-hand look at the mechanics behind the 'recursive self-improvement' talking point.

item.title: What Huawei's Horinger data center reveals about China's compute gap (Epoch AI)
item.description: Uses satellite images of cooling equipment, substations and generators to estimate one of China's largest AI data centres: about 286 MW and roughly 81,000 H100-equivalents, about 7 percent of SpaceX's Colossus 2 in Tennessee. Explains in real numbers why abundant Chinese power does not close the gap when domestic chips deliver far less compute per watt.
